events.title: The first apparition at Lourdes
events.shortBlurb: At a grotto in the Pyrenees the Blessed Virgin first appeared to Bernadette Soubirous, calling for prayer and penance…
body: Bernadette Soubirous was the eldest child of a ruined miller, her family lodging in a disused prison cell called the Cachot, when on 11 February 1858 she went with her sister and a friend to gather firewood along the Gave de Pau. At the hollow of Massabielle she heard a sound like a gust of wind and saw in a niche a lady dressed in white.

Neither her parents nor the parish priest, Abbé Dominique Peyramale, believed her at first, and as the crowds grew the civil power moved against the grotto: the police commissioner Jacomet questioned her repeatedly, and in the summer of 1858 officials fenced off the spring under penalty for trespassers. The quarrel became national, and Emperor Napoleon III himself ordered the barriers removed that October.

The Bishop of Tarbes held aloof from the fray, naming a canonical commission in November 1858 that for three years examined the child, the witnesses, and the reported cures. Only on 18 January 1862 did Bishop Laurence pronounce the apparitions 'supernatural and divine.' The skepticism that had fenced the grotto thus gave way to a judgment all the firmer for its delay.

events.title: The Lateran Treaty and the birth of Vatican City
events.shortBlurb: An agreement between the Holy See and Italy settled the “Roman Question” and created the sovereign State of Vatican City…
body: On 11 February 1929 the Lateran Pacts were signed in the Lateran Palace at Rome, ending the Roman Question that had divided the papacy from Italy since the seizure of Rome in 1870. For Pope Pius XI signed his Secretary of State, Cardinal Pietro Gasparri, and for King Victor Emmanuel III the head of the government, Benito Mussolini, after nearly three years of negotiation.

The pacts comprised a political treaty, a financial convention, and a concordat. The treaty recognized the full sovereignty of the Holy See over the new State of Vatican City, a territory of some forty-four hectares around St. Peter's; the convention compensated the loss of the Papal States with 750 million lire and a further billion in state bonds; the concordat regulated the life of the Church in Italy.

The settlement freed the papacy from the self-imposed imprisonment of nearly sixty years and secured its independence of any earthly power. Ratified on 7 June 1929, the treaty was received into the constitution of the Italian Republic in 1948 and, with the concordat revised in 1984, remains the charter of the smallest sovereign state in the world.
